title: Dauphinoise Potatoes
subtitle: Thinly sliced potatoes baked in cream and garlic
excerpt: Thinly sliced floury potatoes layered with garlic and thyme, saturated in double cream, and baked low and slow until the top is golden and the potatoes inside are completely tender. The definitive potato gratin.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gratin dauphinois is a dish from the Dauphine region of south-east France, first recorded in 1788. The classic preparation uses no cheese: the richness comes entirely from cream infused with garlic. Many British versions add Gruyere on top, which browns well and adds flavour. The potatoes must be sliced thinly and evenly and the dish must bake long enough for the cream to be fully absorbed. A mandoline makes the slicing faster and more consistent.

recipeTools.notes: Or a wide, deep oven-proof dish.
Optional but gives more even slices.

content.text: Slice the potatoes no thicker than 3 mm: if they are thicker, the outside overcooks before the centre softens. Do not rinse the sliced potatoes or the starch washes away, and it is the starch that thickens the cream into a sauce. Test for doneness by pressing a knife into the centre of the dish: the potatoes should offer no resistance at all.

Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Rub a large roasting dish generously with butter. Warm the cream, garlic, and thyme sprigs together in a saucepan until just below simmering. Remove the thyme. Season the cream well with salt and pepper.
Layer the sliced potatoes in the dish, slightly overlapping. Pour the cream over the top, pressing the potatoes gently to submerge them. Scatter the Gruyere over the surface.

Cover tightly with foil. Bake for 60 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for a further 25 to 30 minutes until the top is deep golden and a knife slides through the potatoes with no resistance. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
